Lauren / Marissa —

Quick legal read below (high-level; circle back if you want a longer memo):

Bottom-line: we can accept a hybrid approach that preserves our operational objectives while limiting precedent risk. Proposed position (short):

- Governing law: New York law (familiar body, commercial contracts). If BlueHarbor will not budge on "Delaware", prefer to remain firm on one of the major commercial jurisdictions (New York or Delaware).

- Forum & dispute resolution: propose arbitration for substantive disputes (ICDR/AAA, seat New York) but explicitly carve out emergency/provisional relief so either party may seek urgent injunctive or preservative relief in a court of competent jurisdiction prior to or during arbitration. Typical carveout language: "Notwithstanding the agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction, and such requests shall not be deemed incompatible with the arbitration agreement."

- Why: arbitration reduces litigation cost/risk and aligns with our standard MSA precedent. The provisional-relief carveout addresses BlueHarbor's practical concern about speed/enforceability of interim measures. It avoids conceding exclusive in-court jurisdiction (which is precedent-y and costly for Redwood).

- Narrow the carveout: add a short list of categories where emergency relief is available (e.g., intellectual property, unauthorized data access, breach of confidentiality). That reduces open-ended forum shopping.

If Sales is willing to accept New York law + arbitration seat New York with a limited injunctive carveout (and a clause requiring immediate escalation to our Security team + written notice), I think it's an acceptable compromise.

Actionable: if you want, I'll draft a counter clause this morning and a 1-paragraph legal rationale for you to forward to BlueHarbor counsel.

Maya —

Thanks for sending these along and for the context. We've reviewed internally and propose the following compromise to avoid a protracted back-and-forth:

1) Governing law: New York law to govern the agreement language (we find it neutral and commercially predictable). If BlueHarbor cannot accept New York law, Redwood is willing to consider Delaware law only if the exclusive-forum request is narrowed as below.

2) Dispute resolution & provisional relief: arbitration for substantive disputes (ICDR/AAA, seat New York). Notwithstanding arbitration, either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction for a limited set of categories (intellectual property infringement, unauthorized access/exfiltration of customer data, and preservation of evidence). Such requests shall not be deemed to waive the agreement to arbitrate.

3) Narrowing & reciprocity: to prevent open-ended forum shopping, the emergency relief carveout will be limited to the categories above and we will include a requirement to notify the other party and Redwood's Security team within 24 hours of seeking any emergency relief. If BlueHarbor insists on exclusive Delaware courts for all disputes, Redwood will need reciprocal concessions (for example, narrow subject matter for exclusive jurisdiction and a mutual expedited discovery protocol).

Markus will follow up with proposed contract language. If this is acceptable in principle, can procurement confirm by EOD Friday so we can finalize and get a countersigned MSA on the books? Happy to do a quick call if that accelerates.

Best,
Lauren
